title: Membranous nephropathy

steps.tx: Autoantibodies against the M-type **phospholipase A2 receptor** (anti-PLA2R, predominantly IgG4 subclass) account for 70% to 80% of primary membranous nephropathy cases, correlating closely with disease activity, remission, and relapse. The image is membranous nephropathy histopathology showing diffuse capillary wall thickening.

steps.tx: Thrombospondin type-1 domain-containing 7A (**THSD7A**), neural epidermal growth factor-like 1 (NELL-1, frequently malignancy-associated), and exostosin 1 and 2 (EXT1/EXT2, associated with autoimmune disease) represent other specific antigenic targets. The paired value for PLA2R (Phospholipase A2 receptor) is 70% to 80% of primary MN.

steps.tx: Kidney biopsy in membranous nephropathy demonstrates diffuse glomerular basement membrane thickening on light microscopy, granular IgG along the capillary loop and C3 on immunofluorescence, and subepithelial electron-dense deposits with intervening **spike-and-dome** GBM projections. The image is silver methenamine staining demonstrating spike and dome patterns.

steps.tx: The **MENTOR** trial established that B-cell depletion with rituximab (1000 mg IV on days 1 and 15) is non-inferior to cyclosporine at 12 months and superior in maintaining complete or partial remission through 24 months. The first step is Baseline high anti-PLA2R antibody titer.

nodes.label: Clinical remission (proteinuria drops 3 to 6 months later)

steps.tx: The **modified** Ponticelli regimen alternates oral/IV corticosteroids with oral cyclophosphamide monthly for 6 months, reserved for patients with very high-risk disease (rapidly declining eGFR or life-threatening nephrotic complications). The paired value for Months 1, 3, and 5 is IV Methylprednisolone pulses then oral corticosteroids.

steps.tx: **KDIGO** risk stratification of membranous nephropathy is low risk (normal eGFR, proteinuria < 3.5 g/day, anti-PLA2R negative), moderate risk, high risk (proteinuria > 8 g/day or anti-PLA2R > 50 RU/mL), and very high risk. One side is Rituximab Protocol, and the other side is Cyclosporine Protocol.
steps.say: KDIGO risk stratification of membranous nephropathy is low risk (normal eGFR, proteinuria less than 3 point 5 g/day, anti-PLA2R negative), moderate risk, high risk (proteinuria greater than 8 g/day or anti-PLA2R greater than 50 RU/mL), and very high risk. One side is Rituximab Protocol, and the other side is Cyclosporine Protocol.

left.title: Rituximab Protocol
points: 1 g on days 1 and 15 or 375 mg/m2 weekly x 4

steps.tx: **Secondary membranous** nephropathy causes include systemic lupus erythematosus (Class V lupus nephritis), solid organ malignancies (carcinoma of lung, colon, stomach, breast), chronic hepatitis B infection, and drugs (NSAIDs, penicillamine, gold). The paired value for Class V lupus nephritis is Subepithelial immune complexes with C1q.

steps.tx: Serial monitoring of anti-PLA2R antibody titers allows immunological monitoring: antibody disappearance (**immunological remission**) precedes clinical reduction in proteinuria (clinical remission) by a median of 3 to 6 months. The first step is Severe nephrotic syndrome with massive proteinuria. The next step is Serum albumin drops below 2.0 to 2.5 g/dL.
